study.notes: STUDY: LYDIA (liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily vs sitagliptin 100 mg once daily, 26 weeks, adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity; head to head trial of two incretin based therapies, a DPP-4 inhibitor comparator, decision D-X7 for the Director on whether an incretin pathway comparator is admissible as a concurrent control); this paper reports the prespecified secondary vascular biomarker analyses (full text, institutional route, group 165); Table 2 gives the mean change (95% CI) per arm and the between group difference liraglutide minus sitagliptin (95% CI) with p from generalized linear models (route ci_95); Table 1 baselines mean (SD); n with data per row (28 and 33); weight change is in the LYDIA primary paper, not here (pct_weight_change empty); NIHR Leicester funding (industry_funded FALSE); rob_overall some_concerns

rows.notes: Table 2: CRP (printed as mg/mL, read as mg/L) change -1.58 (-5.75 to 2.64) liraglutide vs -0.99 (-5.04 to 3.04) sitagliptin, between group difference -0.56 (-6.76 to 5.65), p = .860; CRP by Quantikine ELISA (not a high sensitivity assay by name), recorded under hsCRP; baseline Table 1 7.4 (8.9) vs 8.0 (1.3)

Table 2: TNF-alpha change -0.01 (-0.08 to 0.06) vs -0.03 (-0.09 to 0.04), between group difference -0.02 (-0.09 to 0.13), p = .711; the printed interval is not symmetric around the estimate (a misprint in the paper), the standard error is taken from the interval width; baseline Table 1 1.4 (0.4) vs 1.4 (0.2)
Table 2: IL-6 change -0.03 (-0.86 to 0.79) vs -0.41 (-1.20 to 0.39), between group difference 0.38 (-0.84 to 1.59), p = .540, unfavourable sign, null; baseline Table 1 2.5 (2.1) vs 2.5 (3.4)

json.design: randomised open label head to head trial, liraglutide vs sitagliptin, 26 weeks, prespecified secondary biomarker analyses (n 28 and 33 with samples)
json.reason: full text group; three inventory markers with between group differences and intervals; the comparator is a DPP-4 inhibitor (D-X7)
other_markers: HbA1c, lipids and weight at baseline only (Table 1); changes in the LYDIA primary paper

rob.justification: S: randomised trial (LYDIA, D1 low by the primary report); open label (D2 some concerns); biomarker samples available for 28 and 33 of the randomised participants, missing data handled by the generalized linear models with no imputation described (D3 some concerns); laboratory ELISA outcomes (D4 low); prespecified secondary outcomes (D5 low)

doubts: DPP-4 inhibitor comparator (sitagliptin): an incretin pathway control, admissibility is decision D-X7
the TNF-alpha interval is asymmetric around its estimate in the paper
dose and blinding taken from the abstract sentence of this secondary paper; the primary LYDIA report is not in this packet
